title: From manual calculations to a working production platform.
summary: A custom incentive system that gives production, managers and HR a defined path from entry to approval.
challenge: A cable manufacturer needed production-incentive calculations and approvals to work across departments. Spreadsheet-based work made the roles, rules and reporting requirements difficult to manage consistently.
judgement: The software had to represent the actual rules of the operation. Production users, IT, managers and HR needed their responsibilities translated into a workflow they could review and use.
work: Six operational modules with their own entry and calculation requirements.
A five-level approval workflow and role-based access.
Department reporting and a documented process for changes.
result: The platform was implemented and confirmed active in writing by the client. It provides a concrete example of custom software built around a business process.
note: An owner-confirmed estimate puts annual repetitive work capacity released at approximately 876 person-days, using 6 × 365 × 0.40. This is an assumption-based capacity estimate, not a measured cash saving. Client identity is withheld.
lesson: Agree the users, rules, exceptions and approval responsibilities together. A feature list alone does not describe the operation.

title: Following the journey all the way to the appointment.
summary: A five-city campaign measured enquiries, appointments and patients, giving the team a more useful view than lead volume alone.
challenge: A multi-city specialty healthcare network needed to understand which enquiries progressed to appointments and patients, and where follow-up needed attention.
judgement: The initial enquiry is only one stage. Campaign reporting becomes more useful when it is connected to the outcomes recorded by the clinic team.
work: Meta lead-generation campaigns across five cities.
Education-led messaging appropriate to the specialist offering.
City-level tracking from enquiry to appointment and patient outcome.
result: The documented campaign window recorded ₹41,121 in media spend, 670 enquiries, 45 appointments and 16 patients: approximately ₹61 per enquiry across the campaign.
note: Appointment and patient outcomes were tracked manually with clinic staff. These describe one campaign window and are not guaranteed future results. Client identity and individual patient records are withheld.
lesson: Define each stage and review the full journey. A low enquiry cost is useful only in the context of what happens next.

title: Reach the plot owner with the right conversation.
summary: A lead-generation approach that used plot size to bring more useful context into the first enquiry.
challenge: A construction-planning and design practice wanted to reach people preparing to build and understand the context of their projects earlier.
judgement: A name and phone number do not explain a building project. A relevant qualifying question can make the first conversation more useful.
work: Campaign messaging directed at plot owners considering construction.
Lead forms segmented by plot size.
An enquiry structure that brought basic project context to the team.
result: The engagement generated approximately 400 enquiries at around ₹60 per enquiry. No sales, project-close or revenue conversion rate is claimed here.
note: Enquiry count and cost are approximate first-party figures. An enquiry is not a signed construction project. Client identity and lead records remain private.
lesson: Ask the question that changes the first sales conversation. Qualification should reflect how your business evaluates a project.

title: A property journey built around the site visit.
summary: Brand identity, a website and campaign journeys brought together for a premium property channel partner.
challenge: A premium property business needed a credible identity and a consistent journey from discovering an offering to enquiring about a site visit.
judgement: The website and the campaign needed to carry the same property story. A buyer should recognise the offer and understand the next step wherever they arrive.
work: A premium brand identity for the business.
A website presenting the property offering.
Meta and Google campaign journeys oriented around a site-visit enquiry.
result: The engagement delivered a brand, website and site-visit funnel. This case demonstrates the delivered system; it does not claim an unverified number of visits or property sales.
note: Client identity is withheld. No lead-to-visit or visit-to-sale percentage is asserted.
lesson: Make each step continue the same conversation. The ad, the property information and the enquiry should agree.

title: Making a distinctive experience easy to understand.
summary: A wellness-tourism concept expressed through its positioning, website and marketing.
challenge: A wellness-tourism and Ayurveda-villa concept needed to explain an unfamiliar offering clearly enough for a prospective guest to consider it.
judgement: The experience itself was the starting point. The website and marketing had to help a guest understand what was being offered and why it was worth choosing.
work: A brand website shaped around the offering.
A coherent story across the agreed marketing work.
result: The owner confirms that an approximately ₹50,000 engagement generated at least ₹2 lakh in business within one month, alongside branding value.
note: Owner-confirmed first-party result from founding-team work. This is business generated from the engagement, not an ad-only return or a guarantee. Client identity is withheld.
lesson: For an unfamiliar offer, clarity is part of the product experience. Help someone picture what they are choosing.

title: Understanding the gap between enquiries and visits.
summary: An anonymised clinic turnaround involving local reputation and the journey from enquiry to walk-in.
challenge: A clinic was receiving enquiries while its real-world visits were suffering after damage to its Google Business Profile and local reputation.
judgement: The task was to understand what happened after the enquiry, including the confidence a prospective patient found when checking the clinic online.
work: Review of the clinic's local digital presence.
Work on the damaged Google Business Profile and trust signals.
Attention to the journey between an enquiry and a clinic visit.
result: The owner confirms that recovery began in approximately 15–21 days and revenue reached around 1.5 times its earlier position within 45 days of onboarding.
note: Owner-confirmed, anonymised result. It is not an independently audited figure or a forecast for another clinic. No star-rating, review-count or medical-outcome claim is made.
lesson: Investigate the decision between interest and arrival. Generating additional enquiries is only one possible response.
